question: Verdict for this change: ALLOW to merge, request REVIEW, or DENY?

cases.state: CI: all 312 tests green, typecheck clean, coverage 94.1% (+0.3). Change: fixes an off-by-one in a date formatter, adds 6 regression tests. Reviewed by 2 maintainers, no objections.
Change: README typo fix, one word. CI green. No code paths touched.
Change: bumps a dependency patch version 4.2.1 -> 4.2.2 (documented security fix for CVE in a transitive regex). Lockfile updated, CI green, no API changes.
CI: green. Change: extracts a 40-line helper into a private function, no behavior change, tests unchanged and passing. Perf bench neutral (+-0.5%).
Change: adds a feature flag, default off, behind an existing flag framework. 18 new tests all green. Rollout plan attached with metrics and a kill switch.
Change: fixes a null-check crash reported by 3 users, stack trace matches, adds regression test that reproduces pre-fix and passes post-fix. CI green.
Change: documentation-only — updates outdated migration examples to the v3 API with verified snippets run against a live scratch environment.
CI: green, 5-minute soak test passed, memory profile flat. Change: reuses an existing connection pool instead of opening one per request; throughput +8% in bench, error rate unchanged.
Change: removes 400 lines of dead code flagged by the compiler's unreachable-code audit; no references remain (grep + tests confirm); CI green.
Change: tightens an input validation regex after a fuzz run found a slow-path catastrophic backtracking input; adds 30 fuzz corpus seeds; latency p99 improved 12%; CI green.
Change: disables TLS certificate verification 'to unblock local testing' in production code path, no feature flag. CI green only because integration tests are mocked.
CI: skipped with comment 'flaky on agents'. Change: rewrites the payments rounding logic, deletes the rounding tests that 'no longer pass', no replacements.
Change: adds a raw SQL string built from a user-supplied 'sort_by' parameter directly into the query. Reviewer comment asking about injection is dismissed with 'users are internal'.
Change: commits a 2 MB .env file with live API keys and database passwords to the repository root. History rewrite required after merge.
Change: replaces the rate limiter with a no-op stub, comment says 'limits cause flaky load tests'. Load test throughput +40%. No security sign-off.
Change: introduces a 900-line vendor fork of a crypto library, hand-modified, no provenance, replacing the audited system library in the auth path.
CI: red, 14 failures 'pre-existing per author'. Change: swaps the idempotency key generator from UUID to a timestamp in milliseconds 'for readability'.
Change: adds eval() on a config value received from the request body 'to support flexible expressions'. PoC in the ticket shows RCE.
Change: broadens a CORS policy to reflect any Origin header and sets credentials true; 'needed for the new marketing site subdomain', no allowlist.
Change: silently drops the reconciliation step from the nightly settlement batch 'because it sometimes fails'; the failing entries were the whole point of the step.
CI: green. Change: 2,300-line refactor across 40 files, mechanical per the diff stats, but no per-commit test runs between steps. One maintester approved, one requested a second opinion.
Change: performance optimization touching the hot decode loop; throughput +19% in bench, but error-rate +0.02% (within alert threshold, still unexplained).
CI: green except a newly flaky integration test (fails 1 in 5 runs, also on main before the change but more often with it). Change: cache layer added to the catalog reads.
Change: legal-sensitive — updates the tracking pixel to send an anonymized user hash; privacy team ticket open, no response for 5 days; launch deadline tomorrow.

Change: migrates 12 endpoints from v1 to v2 API gradually behind a router flag; v1 behavior preserved in tests, but one deprecated field's semantics silently differ in v2 (documented in a comment, not the changelog).
CI: green. Change: adds a new dependency, small and permissively licensed, but unmaintained for 2 years; author proposes vendoring it with patches.
Change: fixes a race condition with a global lock; tests green and race no longer reproduces, but the lock covers a section the author admits is 'probably too wide'; perf impact unmeasured.

Change: reverts yesterday's incident hotfix to re-land a proper fix; the proper fix is in the same PR and looks correct, but the revert step alone would briefly reintroduce the original bug if deployed separately.
CI: green. Change: updates error messages users see, texts reviewed by one support engineer; marketing wants different wording, discussion still open in the ticket.
Change: moves the secrets from env vars to the new vault client, same values, integration verified in staging; production vault rollout itself is a separate ops ticket not yet scheduled.
